ps30aug1808.summary: John Armstrong, US minister in France, tells Madison in a coded postscript that Russel (most probably Jonathan Russell) ought to be the consul, being American-born and better qualified than any other candidate, and that O'Mealy comes next but is, like Warden, an Irishman: the same animus against David Bailie Warden that led Armstrong to remove him in 1810.
ps30aug1808.en:
P.S. Russel ought to be the consul: he is an American by birth, and is much better qualifi[ed] than any other
candidate. In a word he is above men in general. Next to him in fitness is O'Mealy, but he is like Warden an
Irish[?man].

snip.cap: The coded postscript of Armstrong to Madison, 30 August 1808
